claim_checks.claim: Host: the LLM application. It creates and manages client instances, enforces security policy and consent, and coordinates the LLM.

claim_checks.claim: Client: a connector created by the host. Each client talks to exactly one server (1:1).
claim_checks.page_says: A host application creates and manages multiple clients, with each client having a 1:1 relationship with a particular server.

claim_checks.claim: In 2026-07-28 the client attaches protocol version and capabilities to every request.
claim_checks.page_says: Attaches protocol version and capabilities to every request

claim_checks.claim: Server: a process or remote service that exposes resources, tools and prompts, and may ask the client for input.
claim_checks.page_says: Expose resources, tools and prompts via MCP primitives ... Request client input (e.g. elicitation1) via InputRequiredResult within a reply ... Can be local processes or remote services

claim_checks.claim: Design principle: servers should not be able to read the whole conversation or "see into" other servers; the host keeps full history and controls cross-server interaction.
claim_checks.page_says: Servers should not be able to read the whole conversation, nor “see into” other servers ... Full conversation history stays with the host
claim_checks.note: The page also says 'Cross-server interactions are controlled by the host'.

claim_checks.claim: All messages follow JSON-RPC 2.0 and are UTF-8.
claim_checks.page_says: [7] All messages between MCP clients and servers MUST follow the JSON-RPC 2.0 specification. [8] JSON-RPC messages MUST be UTF-8 encoded.

claim_checks.claim: Request: id is a string or integer, must not be null, must not repeat while another request with that id is unanswered.
claim_checks.page_says: Requests MUST include a string or integer ID. ... The request ID MUST NOT match the ID of any other request the sender has issued
claim_checks.note: 'the ID MUST NOT be null' and '... and not yet received a response for' are on the page too.

claim_checks.claim: Response: error.code is an integer; in 2026-07-28 every result must carry resultType ("complete" or "input_required"); an absent resultType from an older server is treated as "complete".
claim_checks.page_says: Error codes MUST be integers. ... The result MUST include a resultType field ... clients MUST treat an absent resultType as "complete".
claim_checks.note: The parentheses list the core values only; [7] also lets extensions add ResultType values. Not a stronger claim, since the doc does not say 'only'.

claim_checks.claim: Notification: method, optional params, no id; the receiver must not reply.
claim_checks.page_says: Notifications are sent from the client to the server or vice versa, as a one-way message. The receiver MUST NOT send a response.
claim_checks.note: 'Notifications MUST NOT include an ID' is also on the page.

claim_checks.claim: 2026-07-28 error codes reserved by the spec: -32020 HeaderMismatch, -32021 MissingRequiredClientCapability, -32022 UnsupportedProtocolVersion.
claim_checks.page_says: -32020 | HeaderMismatch ... -32021 | MissingRequiredClientCapability ... -32022 | UnsupportedProtocolVersion

claim_checks.section: ### 1.4 Legacy lifecycle (2025-11-25 and earlier): initialize, operate, shutdown
claim_checks.claim: Three phases.
claim_checks.page_says: Initialization: Capability negotiation and protocol version agreement ... Operation: Normal protocol communication ... Shutdown: Graceful termination of the connection
claim_checks.note: The claim is right, but the numbered list under it has five items and never names the Operation phase (a structure issue, outside this part's steps).

claim_checks.section: ### 1.4 Legacy lifecycle (2025-11-25 and earlier): initialize, operate, shutdown
claim_checks.claim: Initialization. The client must send initialize with protocolVersion, capabilities, clientInfo. The server must answer with its own protocolVersion, capabilities, serverInfo (and optional instructions). Then the client must send notifications/initialized.
claim_checks.page_says: The client MUST initiate this phase by sending an initialize request containing: ... The server MUST respond with its own capabilities and information
claim_checks.note: 'the client MUST send an initialized notification' is on the page; the response example carries protocolVersion, capabilities, serverInfo and "instructions": "Optional instructions for the client".

claim_checks.section: ### 1.4 Legacy lifecycle (2025-11-25 and earlier): initialize, operate, shutdown
claim_checks.claim: Before the server answers, the client should send nothing but pings; before initialized, the server should send nothing but pings and logging.
claim_checks.page_says: The client SHOULD NOT send requests other than pings before the server has responded to the initialize request.
claim_checks.note: Wider scope: the page restricts only requests, while 'send nothing but pings' also rules out notifications (for example a cancellation) that the page allows. The server rule has the same widening ('SHOULD NOT send requests other than pings and logging'). Fix: 'the client should send no requests other than pings ...; the server should send no requests other than pings and logging ...' [4].

claim_checks.section: ### 1.4 Legacy lifecycle (2025-11-25 and earlier): initialize, operate, shutdown
claim_checks.claim: Version negotiation. The client sends a version it supports (should be its latest). If the server supports it, it must reply with the same version; otherwise it must reply with another version it supports (should be its latest). If the client cannot use that version it should disconnect.
claim_checks.page_says: If the server supports the requested protocol version, it MUST respond with the same version. Otherwise, the server MUST respond with another protocol version it supports.
claim_checks.note: The SHOULD for 'latest' on both sides and the client's SHOULD disconnect are on the page too.

claim_checks.section: ### 1.4 Legacy lifecycle (2025-11-25 and earlier): initialize, operate, shutdown
claim_checks.claim: Capability negotiation. Client capabilities: roots, sampling, elicitation, tasks, experimental. Server capabilities: prompts, resources, tools, logging, completions, tasks, experimental. Sub-flags: listChanged, subscribe (resources only). Both sides must use only capabilities that were negotiated.
claim_checks.page_says: subscribe: Support for subscribing to individual items’ changes (resources only) ... Both parties MUST: ... Only use capabilities that were successfully negotiated
claim_checks.note: The capability table on the page lists exactly these client and server capabilities.

claim_checks.section: ### 1.4 Legacy lifecycle (2025-11-25 and earlier): initialize, operate, shutdown
claim_checks.claim: Shutdown. No shutdown message exists. On stdio the client closes the server's stdin, waits, then sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL if needed. On HTTP, closing the connection(s) ends it.
claim_checks.page_says: Waiting for the server to exit, or sending SIGTERM if the server does not exit within a reasonable time ... shutdown is indicated by closing the associated HTTP connection(s).
claim_checks.note: The page's steps are a SHOULD and SIGTERM is conditional on the server not exiting; the doc's 'waits ... if needed' carries that condition, if loosely.

claim_checks.section: ### 1.4 Legacy lifecycle (2025-11-25 and earlier): initialize, operate, shutdown
claim_checks.claim: Timeouts. Implementations should time out every request and then send a cancellation notification; progress may reset the clock but a maximum timeout should always apply.
claim_checks.page_says: the sender SHOULD issue a cancellation notification for that request ... implementations SHOULD always enforce a maximum timeout, regardless of progress notifications
claim_checks.note: Modal verbs match: SHOULD, MAY reset, SHOULD enforce a maximum.

claim_checks.section: ### 1.4 Legacy lifecycle (2025-11-25 and earlier): initialize, operate, shutdown
claim_checks.claim: Version negotiation (experiment E2): the same server was sent protocolVersion "1.0.0" and answered "2025-11-25", matching the "respond with another supported version" rule.
claim_checks.page_says: Otherwise, the server MUST respond with another protocol version it supports.
claim_checks.note: The rule is on [4]. The observed exchange rests on E2 (local, not checkable).

claim_checks.claim: "There is no negotiation handshake." Every request carries its protocol version, and the server accepts or rejects each request on its own.
claim_checks.page_says: There is no negotiation handshake. Every request carries its protocol version, and the server accepts or rejects each request independently
claim_checks.note: The quote is exact.

claim_checks.claim: Every request carries these _meta keys: io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion (required), io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities (required), io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo (optional, but clients should send it).
claim_checks.page_says: fields marked as required MUST be included on every request. ... Clients SHOULD include io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo on every request unless specifically configured not to do so.
claim_checks.note: The page's table marks protocolVersion and clientCapabilities 'Yes' and clientInfo 'No'.

claim_checks.claim: A request missing a required key is rejected with -32602, and with HTTP 400 on HTTP.
claim_checks.page_says: A request missing any required field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code -32602 (Invalid params). On HTTP, the response status MUST be 400 Bad Request.

claim_checks.claim: A server that does not support the requested version must answer UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (code -32022) listing data.supported; the client should retry with a mutually supported version.
claim_checks.page_says: it MUST respond with an UnsupportedProtocolVersionError listing the versions it does support ... The client SHOULD select a mutually supported version from the supported list and retry the request
claim_checks.note: The example on the page shows "code": -32022 and data.supported.

claim_checks.claim: A server that needs a client capability the request did not declare must return -32021 with data.requiredCapabilities.
claim_checks.page_says: the server MUST return a MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (-32021) whose data.requiredCapabilities lists the missing capabilities.

claim_checks.claim: Servers must implement server/discover, which returns supportedVersions, capabilities, optional instructions and _meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]. Clients may call it first, but are not required to.
claim_checks.page_says: Servers MUST implement it. ... Calling server/discover is optional for clients
claim_checks.note: The DiscoverResult list on the page has supportedVersions, capabilities, _meta serverInfo (SHOULD) and optional instructions. On stdio, a dual-era client SHOULD send it first; the doc's general statement still holds.

claim_checks.claim: Servers must not rely on earlier requests on the same connection for context (statelessness). State that spans requests must be an explicit identifier the client passes on each request.
claim_checks.page_says: Servers MUST NOT rely on prior requests over the same connection to establish context ... MUST be referenced by an explicit identifier the client passes on each request.

claim_checks.claim: An open connection (for example a stdio process) is not a conversation or session.
claim_checks.page_says: This implies that an open connection, such as a STDIO process, is not a conversation or session

claim_checks.claim: Shutdown on stdio: close the server's stdin, wait, then force-terminate if needed; servers should exit when stdin closes.
claim_checks.page_says: If the server does not exit within a reasonable time, forcibly terminating the process ... Servers SHOULD exit promptly when their standard input is closed

claim_checks.claim: On HTTP there is nothing to shut down: each request is its own POST.
claim_checks.page_says: The client sends every JSON-RPC request or notification as its own HTTP POST.
claim_checks.note: Searched [13] for 'shut', 'teardown', 'tear down': not found. The page supports one POST per request and no sessions, but never says HTTP needs no shutdown, and it describes a subscriptions/listen response stream 'that stays open'. [15], not cited here, says the client ends one by closing the SSE stream. Fix: 'On HTTP there is no session to end; close any open subscriptions/listen stream, since closing it cancels the subscription' [13][15].

claim_checks.claim: Extensions (for example Tasks io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks, MCP Apps) are negotiated through an extensions map in capabilities.
claim_checks.page_says: Extensions are advertised in the extensions field of capabilities, which is a map of extension identifiers to per-extension settings objects.
claim_checks.note: The page's examples name the MCP Apps extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/ui) and Tasks (io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks).

claim_checks.claim: Same session, modern era (experiment E4, SDK 2.4.0, serveStdio): the wire transcript shown.
claim_checks.page_says: not checked: cites only the local experiment E4

claim_checks.claim: The missing-_meta error and the -32022 shape match the spec.
claim_checks.page_says: [7] the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code -32602 (Invalid params) [5] "code": -32022, ... "supported": ["2026-07-28", "2025-11-25"], "requested": "1900-01-01"
claim_checks.note: Compared against the E4 lines as printed in the doc. [5]'s matrix also says the error code for a rejected initialize on stdio is implementation-defined, so returning -32022 there is allowed.

claim_checks.claim: Step 2, Negotiate, legacy (2025-11-25): initialize request, response, notifications/initialized.
claim_checks.page_says: After successful initialization, the client MUST send an initialized notification to indicate it is ready to begin normal operations:

claim_checks.claim: Step 2, Negotiate, current (2026-07-28): optional server/discover; version and capabilities ride in each request's _meta.
claim_checks.page_says: [11] Calling server/discover is optional for clients [7] Every request supplies this metadata in its _meta field.

claim_checks.claim: Step 3, List tools, legacy (2025-11-25): tools/list.
claim_checks.page_says: To discover available tools, clients send a tools/list request.
claim_checks.note: Wrong era: [14] is the 2026-07-28 tools page, and searching it for '2025-11-25', 'legacy' and 'earlier revision' finds nothing, so it does not cover the legacy column. Fix: cite the 2025-11-25 tools page (no saved text in this input) or mark the cell with the unverified symbol.

claim_checks.claim: Step 3, List tools, current (2026-07-28): tools/list plus _meta; result has ttlMs and cacheScope.
claim_checks.page_says: This operation supports pagination and caching. ... "ttlMs": 300000, "cacheScope": "public"
claim_checks.note: The page also says 'Every request MUST include the required _meta fields'.

claim_checks.claim: Step 4, Call a tool, current (2026-07-28): tools/call plus _meta; result has resultType.
claim_checks.page_says: Every request MUST include the required _meta fields ... "resultType": "complete",
claim_checks.note: resultType appears in the tools/call response example.

claim_checks.claim: Step 5, React to changes, legacy (2025-11-25): notifications/tools/list_changed, delivered on a GET stream or the open connection.
claim_checks.page_says: [4] This can be used to open an SSE stream [13] clients could open a standalone SSE stream with HTTP GET to receive server-initiated messages
claim_checks.note: [4] also gives listChanged as tools list-change support and the stdio server writing to stdout. The exact method name appears only in 2026-07-28 text ([13] line on subscriptions/listen); no cached legacy page spells it. Minor cross-era gap, so this passes with a caveat.

claim_checks.claim: Step 5, React to changes, current (2026-07-28): open subscriptions/listen with toolsListChanged:true; server acks with notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged.
claim_checks.page_says: [15] The server MUST send notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged as the first message carrying the subscription’s ID ... toolsListChanged | boolean | Receive notifications/tools/list_changed when tools change

claim_checks.claim: Step 6, Shut down, legacy (2025-11-25): stdio: close stdin, SIGTERM, SIGKILL. HTTP: close connection, optionally DELETE with the session id.
claim_checks.page_says: Clients that no longer need a particular session (e.g., because the user is leaving the client application) SHOULD send an HTTP DELETE to the MCP endpoint with the MCP-Session-Id header
claim_checks.note: The page says SHOULD when a session exists; 'optionally' fits because the server MAY assign a session at all. [16] resolves to [4].

claim_checks.claim: Step 6, Shut down, current (2026-07-28): stdio: close stdin, then force. HTTP: nothing to do.
claim_checks.page_says: [12] Closing the input stream to the child process (the server). [13] not found: searched 'shut', 'teardown', 'tear down'
claim_checks.note: The stdio half is supported. 'HTTP: nothing to do' has the same gap as C39: [13] never says it and describes long-lived subscriptions/listen streams that stay open. Fix: 'HTTP: close any open subscriptions/listen stream; there is no session to end' [13][15].
